item.title: A Bicriteria Approximation Scheme for the Minimum Well-Separated Pair Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2610.13650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A well-separated pair decomposition (WSPD) of a set $P$ of $n$ points covers all $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs of points by a family of dumbbells $\{X,Y\}$, each covering the pairs of $X\times Y$, such that the diameters of $X$ and $Y$ are at most an $\varepsilon$-fraction of their distance. In $\mathbb{R}^d$, WSPDs with $O(n/\varepsilon^d)$ dumbbells always exist, but many inputs admit much smaller ones. However, computing a WSPD of minimum size is NP-hard in the plane. For $d\ge2$, the only known approximation that preserves the separation has a factor of $2^{O(d)}$, and Buchin et al. (ESA 2026) asked whether a $(1+\delta)$-approximation exists. We give a bicriteria approximation scheme: for fixed $d$ and $\delta\in(0,1]$, we compute in $f(d,\delta)\cdot n^{6}$ time a $(1+\delta)\varepsilon$-WSPD whose size is at most $(1+\delta)$ times the minimum size of an $\varepsilon$-WSPD. The same holds in metric spaces of bounded doubling dimension. The algorithm combines shifting over scales with the local-growth technique of Nieberg, Hurink, and Kern, applied to a graph whose vertices are the pairs of points. In contrast, we show that in general metric spaces, relaxing the separation by a factor below $2$ keeps the problem hard: for every fixed rational $\varepsilon\le1/4$, it is NP-hard to compute such a relaxed WSPD whose size is within a factor $n^c$ of the minimum, for every $c<2/3$.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme D. da Fonseca

item.title: Spherical Geometrical Bases of Spherical Origami
item.description: arXiv:2605.01184v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper establishes a rigorous geometrical framework for spherical origami (origami using spherical sheets based on spherical geometry) in two settings: origami restricted to the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$, and three-dimensional folding of spherical sheets in space. Three main results are proved. First, all seven Huzita--Justin axioms admit explicit constructions on $\mathbb{S}^2$, so spherical origami inherits the same one-fold axiom structure as Euclidean origami. Second, the Kawasaki--Justin theorem on flat-foldability extends to $\mathbb{S}^2$ by a local-tangent-plane argument, and the resulting vertex condition is equivalent to the angle-sum condition that characterizes Robertson's spherical $f$-tilings. Third, taking equidistant curves (small arcs) as fold curves yields a one-parameter family of isometric 3D folds, parametrized by the dihedral angle whose closed-form expression is derived, and recovers geodesic folds as the flat limit. The framework is illustrated by constructing computer graphics of spherical origami birds as a concrete example.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Yoshino
